hook: This is a short entry built around a single 33-second loop, laid out as a second-by-second timeline. Read the steps slowly rather than skimming, because each small action is a clue. The last stage describes a man's body being torn apart in some detail.
whyItMatters:
1033 shows how much story a strict timeline format can carry. There is no interview and no incident log, only a balding man in a business suit repeating the same half minute forever, and the reader is left to work out what that half minute was.

It also leans on loose ends the Foundation cannot follow up: a cipher phrase, a sealed envelope and a phone number that does not yet belong to anyone.
thingsToNotice:
The loop plays out like the final moments before a strike: he checks his watch, reads a coded instruction, texts a string of characters to an unassigned Australian number, then gazes toward the horizon and laughs softly as if he has found what he was waiting for. Seconds later he is thrown back and stripped apart with injuries that match a 1.5 megaton nuclear detonation, then reappears mid-step to begin again.

The arrival details fit the same picture: a blinding white flash, a burst of static from every direction, and radiation far past lethal levels. Notice too that he never reacts to anything placed in front of him; he simply pushes obstacles along, which is why a shipping container in his path was enough to catch him.
